standards.applies_because: Particular requirements for appliances for skin or hair care (hair dryers)
EMC emissions of the fan motor and heater control
US household electric personal grooming appliances (with immersion protection / ALCI plug)

risks.risk: Heater overheats when the intake is blocked (hair, towel)
risks.mitigation: Thermal cut-out + one-shot thermal fuse on the heater, intake filter with a stand-off
Immersion protection (ALCI/GFCI plug in the US, RCD guidance in the EU), IEC 60335-2-23 warnings

risks.risk: Outlet air too hot for the scalp at max setting
risks.mitigation: Closed-loop outlet temperature (NTC) and a cool-shot button

risks.risk: Noise: a 'quiet' claim fails with a small high-speed fan
risks.mitigation: Larger, slower fan; acoustic foam at the intake; measure dB(A) at 0.5 m early
Swivel cord exit and flex test to the standard

tests.name: Temperature rise and abnormal operation (blocked intake)
tests.method: Run with the intake blocked until the cut-out operates

tests.name: Outlet air temperature at 3 cm, each setting
tests.method: Thermocouple grid in front of the nozzle

tests.name: Drop test
tests.method: Drops onto a hard floor per the standard

tests.name: Cord flex test
tests.method: Flexing test of the supply cord

prototype.method: SLA high-temperature resin (nozzle, barrel) + MJF PA12 (handle), bought-in heater and fan
steps: Bench the heater + fan module in a printed duct, map outlet temperature vs setting
Print the body in heat-resistant SLA resin and MJF PA12
Wire through a bought-in thermal cut-out and fuse before any user test
Blocked-intake test until the cut-out operates
Noise measurement at 0.5 m per setting
